parts.gloss: those who are worthy of being begged from

words.gloss: those who are worthy of being begged from

literal: One may beg, those worthy of being begged from if one sees; if they withhold, their blame, one's own blame it is not.
translation: One may beg if they meet those who are worthy of giving; if those givers withhold their wealth, the blame is theirs, not the beggar's.
modern: இரந்து கேட்பதற்குத் தகுதியானவர்களைக் கண்டால் அவரிடம் இரந்து கேட்கலாம்; அவ்வாறு கேட்டபோது அவர் கொடுக்காமல் மறைத்தால், அது அவருக்குப் பழியே தவிர, கேட்பவருக்குப் பழி அன்று.
explanation: This couplet explains the ethics of asking for help and where the shame of refusal lies. The poet suggests that begging is acceptable if one approaches those who are genuinely worthy and capable of giving. If these wealthy individuals choose to hide their resources and refuse to help, the moral disgrace belongs entirely to them. The person in need who asked for help bears no blame or shame in this situation.
